title: Paella valenciana

ingredients.note: jointed; use extra chicken if unavailable
flat green beans, cut into 4 cm pieces
fresh or cooked large white beans

steps: Heat the oil in a 40 cm paella pan or wide shallow pan over medium-high heat. Season the chicken and rabbit with salt and brown on all sides, about 12 minutes.
Push the meat to the edges, add the green beans and cook for 5 minutes. Add the lima beans.
Make a space in the centre, add the grated tomato and cook for 3 minutes until it darkens, then stir in the paprika for a few seconds.
Pour in the hot water and saffron and bring to a boil. Simmer for about 20 minutes, until the meat is tender, then taste the broth and adjust the salt; it should be a little salty.
Scatter the rice evenly over the pan and do not stir after this. Cook on high for 8 minutes, then medium for 10 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
Turn the heat up for the last minute or two so the bottom toasts slightly, listening for a light crackle. Rest the pan off the heat for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Rice should be about a thumb's depth or less in the pan. Cooking on a stove with a smaller pan will need a lid and slightly more time.

title: Chilled gazpacho
steps: Soak the bread in the water for 5 minutes.
Blend the tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, garlic and soaked bread until completely smooth.
With the blender running, add the vinegar, then slowly pour in the oil so it emulsifies to a pale orange colour. Season with salt.
Pass through a fine sieve for a smoother soup, then chill for at least 2 hours.
Taste again when cold and adjust salt and vinegar. Serve in glasses or bowls with a drizzle of oil.
notes: Serve with chopped cucumber, pepper and bread as optional garnishes.

title: Tortilla de patatas
steps: Warm the oil in a 24 cm non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Add the potatoes and onion with a good pinch of salt and cook gently for about 20 minutes, turning occasionally, until soft but not coloured.
Drain the potatoes in a sieve over a bowl, keeping the oil.
Beat the eggs in a large bowl with a little salt, fold in the warm potatoes and onion and leave for 5 minutes.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the reserved oil in the pan over medium heat, pour in the mixture and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the edges set.
Place a large plate over the pan, flip the tortilla out, slide it back in and cook the other side for 3 to 4 minutes, keeping the centre slightly soft.
Rest for 5 minutes before cutting.
notes: Leave out the onion for the purist version. Keep the leftover oil for cooking.

title: Octopus with potatoes and paprika

ingredients.note: cleaned; frozen and thawed octopus is more tender

steps: Bring a large pot of unsalted water to a boil. Holding the octopus by the head, dip the tentacles in and out three times for a few seconds each, then submerge it fully.
Reduce to a simmer and cook for 45 to 60 minutes until a knife slides easily into the thickest part of a tentacle. Turn off the heat and leave in the water for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in their skins in a separate pan with salt for about 25 minutes. Peel and cut into 1 cm slices.
Cut the octopus tentacles into 1 cm slices with scissors.
Arrange the potatoes on a plate, top with the octopus, sprinkle with coarse salt and paprika and drizzle with the oil. Serve warm.
notes: Cooking times vary with the size of the octopus. Do not salt the octopus water.

title: Salt cod pil-pil
steps: Desalt the cod by soaking it skin-side up in cold water in the fridge for 24 to 36 hours, changing the water every 6 to 8 hours. Pat dry.
Warm the oil with the garlic (and chile, if using) in a wide pan over low heat until the garlic turns pale gold, then remove the garlic and set it aside.

Let the oil cool a little, then place the cod pieces skin-side up in the pan and cook very gently for about 5 minutes. Turn them over, skin down, and cook 5 more minutes. The oil should barely bubble.
Take out the cod and let the oil cool slightly, away from the heat.
Return the cod to the pan, skin-side up, and swirl the pan in slow circular motions for 10 minutes, letting the gelatine blend with the oil until it thickens to a creamy sauce.
Serve the cod with the sauce and the reserved garlic.
notes: The sauce needs patience and a gentle motion. If it separates, reduce the temperature and add a spoonful of water while swirling.

title: Pa amb tomàquet
steps: Toast the bread slices in a toaster, on a grill pan or under the grill until crisp at the edges.
Rub the cut side of the garlic, if using, over the warm bread.
Rub the cut side of the tomato firmly over each slice, squeezing so the pulp soaks in, until the bread is wet and red.
Drizzle with olive oil, sprinkle with salt and serve at once.
notes: Serve with cured ham, cheese or anchovies if you like.

title: Castilian garlic soup
steps: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and fry the garlic for 1 to 2 minutes until golden but not brown.
Add the bread and fry for 2 to 3 minutes, then take off the heat and stir in the paprika, which burns easily.
Add the stock, return to the heat and simmer for 15 minutes until the bread breaks down. Season with salt.
Crack the eggs into the soup, cover and cook gently for 3 to 4 minutes until the whites set, or divide into ovenproof bowls and bake at 200 C for 5 minutes.
Serve hot.
notes: Some cooks add a few slices of cured ham with the garlic. Stir the eggs in to thicken if you prefer.

title: Torrijas

ingredients.note: 50 g for the milk and 50 g for coating

steps: Warm the milk with 50 g of the sugar and the lemon zest until the sugar dissolves, then let it cool.
Mix 50 g of sugar with the cinnamon in a shallow dish for coating.
Dip each bread slice in the milk until soaked but not falling apart, about 30 seconds per side, then lay on a rack for a minute to drain.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Dip each slice in beaten egg and fry for 2 minutes per side until golden.
Drain on paper, then roll in the cinnamon sugar while hot. Serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: Some versions are soaked in sweet wine rather than milk, and others are finished with honey.

title: Pestiños with honey
steps: Warm the 60 ml oil gently with the anise seeds and orange zest for 3 minutes, then let it cool.
Mix the flour, sesame seeds and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Add the cooled flavoured oil and the wine and knead into a smooth dough. Rest it, covered, for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough out thinly, about 2 mm, and cut into 6 cm squares. Fold the four corners into the centre and press down lightly.
Heat the frying oil to about 170 C and fry the pestiños in batches for 1 to 2 minutes until golden. Drain on paper.
Warm the honey, water and cinnamon in a pan and simmer for 5 minutes. Dip each pestiño in the syrup, then lay on a rack to set.
notes: The dough should be firm rather than sticky; add a spoonful of wine if it is dry.

title: Pumpkin fritters
steps: Mix the warm water, 1 tablespoon sugar and yeast and leave for 10 minutes until foamy.
Combine the pumpkin, flour, a pinch of salt and the anise in a bowl, add the yeast mixture and beat to a soft, sticky dough.
Cover and let it rise for about 1 hour until almost doubled.
Heat the oil to about 170 C. With oiled hands or two oiled spoons, drop in walnut-sized pieces of dough and fry in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning until golden.
Drain on paper and roll in sugar while warm.
notes: Serve with hot chocolate, honey, or sugar alone.
